extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders submitting public comments on FDA regulation of human drug compounding (industry, health care professionals, consumers, researchers, states)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting information, recommendations, and public comments to the FDA's general docket on human drug compounding (matters under sections 503A and 503B) that are not specific to other FDA dockets or documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of the docket
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA has established a public docket to receive information, recommendations, and comments on matters related to the Agency’s regulation of compounding of human drug products under sections 503A and 503B of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). This docket is intended for general comments related to human drug compounding that are not specific to documents or issues that are the subject of other dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this docket for general matters related to human drug compounding (503A/503B). It is not intended for comment on specific documents or issues already covered in other dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable content types
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders can share information, research, and ideas on any matters related to human drug compounding that are not specific to the documents or issues on which we have already sought public comment in other dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of useful submissions include data, research findings, analyses, and policy ideas relevant to compounding practice and regulation. The docket is for substantive contributions on broad compounding topics rather than comments tied to a particular guidance or rulemaking document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit duplicative comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should not be submitted to this general docket if they have already been submitted to specific dockets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions are duplicative and not helpful to the Agency. If comments on particular documents or issues are submitted to this docket rather than the docket specifically opened for the particular document or issue, the comment might not be considered as the specific documents are being finalized and issues considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA will not respond to questions or requests submitted to this docket
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA will not respond to questions or requests submitted to this docket but will consider any information submitted in its work to implement the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect individualized answers or actions in response to docket submissions; submissions may be considered in FDA's regulatory work but will not generate direct replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket status and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA issued a notice in the Federal Register on March 6, 2015, announcing the open docket. The docket will remain open until further notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The docket is ongoing; check the docket or the page for current status (content current as of 09/25/2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Federal Register notices and Compounding Regulatory Policy Information for specific matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Since enactment of the Drug Quality and Security Act, FDA has sought public comment on a number of specific human drug compounding issues and has published numerous Federal Register notices seeking public input. A complete list of the human drug compounding policy documents issued by the Agency for public comment can be found on the Compounding Regulatory Policy Information web page. The Agency will continue to seek public comment on specific documents and issues through future Federal Register notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your comment pertains to a specific proposed guidance, registration process, product reporting requirement, or nomination (e.g., list of drugs that present demonstrable difficulties for compounding), submit it to the docket or Federal Register notice that was opened for that specific document or issue. The page cites prior examples (78 FR 72899; 78 FR 72897; 78 FR 72840) as illustrations of such targeted notices.
